searchText: Yeah that sounds like an effect that exists Though there are also superlinear costs as well, namely the fact that if your block has a reduced change of being included then you need an even higher fee in the case where it _does_ get included to compensate for non-inclusion risk in expectation I... have no idea which one of those dominates Of course the superlinear cost dominates _eventually_, but not sure what happens at the 12-25M level I guess the superlinear one is small then, because it's only a multiplicative factor of `(1 / (1 - uncle_rate))^2` The `^2` being because I'm taking the derivative to compute _marginal_ cost So maybe the superlinear factor is 10% and the sublinear factor is 10% and we can pretend they cancel out 😋 Doesn't this go away *mostly* in 1559 due to transaction fee rewards being so small? Still matters at infinity, but doesn't matter until something like 1M gas blocks. No, it does not You might be thinking of a different effect, where in a non-EIP-1559 and fee-dominated chain, the minimal uncle-risk-compensating fee goes up in cases where the fees of other transactions are higher In fact, that creates weird mechanics when there is *no* block reward, because it weirdly implies that potentially _any_ fee level can be an equilibrium for partially filled blocks, if uncle risk is too high for miners to be willing to fill the blocks completely Or rather, if there is no block reward, the equilibrium block size depends on the shape of the fee demand curve, and not its magnitude (!!) Fortunately, 1559 does bring us further away from such a strange and unstable world
